Resolved on a later pass, after this was first recorded as not-applicable on a wrong theory. The instruction is followed: `cacheComponents` and `partialPrefetching` are on in next.config.ts, and every non-API route is now partial — `scripts/route-policy.ts` reads 2 static, 22 partial, 0 dynamic. Two changes were needed and both copy the release's own shape (`app/(dashboard)/layout.tsx` and `src/views/console-chrome.tsx`): the shell is rendered from the Server Component layout rather than from a client frame, and the rail, the tools and the palette each resolve their own reads behind their own Suspense boundary with a skeleton fallback. Building the release is what settled it — its own routes are 201 PARTIALLY_STATIC, so the access seam was never what made this work; the boundaries are. The 24 requestDependentRoutes declarations this session added as a workaround are deleted, because the check can now see the build.
